# Setup {.unnumbered}

Before session 2, install two things: Python and the VS Code editor. Then run
a two-line script to check that everything works. 

## 1. Python

We use Python **3.14** from [python.org](https://www.python.org/downloads/).
It comes with IDLE, the simple editor we open in session 2.

::: {.panel-tabset group="os"}

### Windows

1. Download the **Python install manager** from [python.org/downloads/windows](https://www.python.org/downloads/windows/) and install it.
2. Open **Terminal / PowerShell** or **Command Prompt** from the Start menu and type:

   ```powershell
   py install 3.14
   ```

   If it asks whether to add a folder to `PATH` or change other settings,
   accept.
3. Check the installation:

   ```powershell
   py --version
   ```

   It should print `Python 3.14.` followed by a number.

IDLE is now in the Start menu under **Python 3.14 → IDLE (Python 3.14)**.

If the install manager gives you trouble, the same page still offers the
classic **Windows installer (64-bit)** for Python 3.14. On its first screen,
tick **Add python.exe to PATH** before clicking **Install Now**.

### macOS

1. Download the **macOS installer** for the latest Python 3.14 from
   [python.org/downloads/macos](https://www.python.org/downloads/macos/)
   and run it, accepting the defaults.
2. At the end, a Finder window opens the folder **Applications → Python 3.14**.
   Double-click **Install Certificates.command** there; it lets Python
   download files from the internet.
3. Open **Terminal** (in Applications → Utilities) and check the installation:

   ```bash
   python3 --version
   ```

   It should print `Python 3.14.` followed by a number.

IDLE is in **Applications → Python 3.14 → IDLE**.

:::

::: {.callout-note title="Already using conda?"}
If you already work with Anaconda, Miniconda or Miniforge, you can keep it:
create an environment with `conda create -n ars-pythonica python=3.14` and
select it in VS Code ([see section 3](#did-it-work)). The instructions in this book assume the
python.org installation, so details may differ for you.
:::

## 2. VS Code

[VS Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/) is the editor we use from session 2
on. It needs the **Python** extension to run Python code.

::: {.panel-tabset group="os"}

### Windows

1. Download the **Windows User Installer** from
   [code.visualstudio.com/download](https://code.visualstudio.com/download)
   and run it. Keep **Add to PATH** ticked.
2. Open VS Code, press **Ctrl+Shift+X** (Extensions), search for **Python**,
   and install the extension by **Microsoft**.
3. Search for **Jupyter** and install the extension by **Microsoft**, so that VS Code can open Jupyter notebooks (`.ipynb` files).

### macOS

1. Download the **Mac** version from
   [code.visualstudio.com/download](https://code.visualstudio.com/download),
   open the download, and move **Visual Studio Code** into **Applications**.
2. Open VS Code, press **Cmd+Shift+X** (Extensions), search for **Python**,
   and install the extension by **Microsoft**.
3. Search for **Jupyter** and install the extension by **Microsoft**, so that VS Code can open Jupyter notebooks (`.ipynb` files).

:::

::: {.callout-note title="Don't forget about ipykernel"}
When you create or open an `.ipynb` notebook for the first time and run any cell, VS Code may prompt you to install `ipykernel` - this package is necessary to execute Jupyter notebook code. Accept and install.
:::

## 3. Did it work? {#did-it-work}

1. Create a local folder for the course, e.g. `ars-pythonica`, and open it in VS Code
   (**File → Open Folder**).
2. Create a new file `hello.py` in it and type or paste:

   ```python
   greeting = 'χαῖρε, κόσμε'
   print(greeting)
   ```

3. Save the file and click the **▷** button (Run Python File) in the top right
   corner. If VS Code asks for an interpreter, choose **Python 3.14**.

::: {.panel-tabset group="os"}

### Windows

The terminal at the bottom should show:

```markdown
χαῖρε, κόσμε
```

If VS Code can't find Python, press **Ctrl+Shift+P**, run
**Python: Select Interpreter**, and choose **Python 3.14**.

### macOS

The terminal at the bottom should show:

```markdown
χαῖρε, κόσμε
```

If VS Code can't find Python, press **Cmd+Shift+P**, run
**Python: Select Interpreter**, and choose **Python 3.14**.

:::

Check the accents and breathings in both the editor and the terminal. If
something fails, save the error message (copied as text, or a screenshot)
and bring it along so that we can discuss it.
